newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha down, kerosene trade seen picking up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha down, kerosene trade seen picking up.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices slid down in thin afternoon trade on Friday, while kerosene trading started to pick up in northern Japan, where the heating season arrives earlier than the rest of the country, traders said.
Several trading houses were said to have recently imported South Korean kerosene cargoes into Japan's northern island of Hokkaido.
Spot kerosene levels were quoted $1.00 to $1.20 per barrel over the mean of Singapore quotes on a C&F (cost and freight) Japan basis.
The naphtha market was virtually deserted due to a public holiday in South Korea and the summer holidays in Japan.
Japan and South Korea are the two most active players in the regional naphtha market.
Open-spec naphtha was notionally quoted at $205.00/$206.00 per tonne for second-half October arrival, down about $1.50 from late Thursday.
Amid the lack of fresh incentives, naphtha prices in Tokyo simply followed an overnight fall in crude values in New York and London, traders said.
